<div class="project-hero">
  <div>
    <h1>Environmental variation and extra-pair paternity in birds</h1>
    <div class="project-subtitle">A reproducible workflow for a global comparative meta-analysis</div>
    <div class="project-hero-meta">
      <div class="project-meta-item">
        <span class="project-meta-label">Author</span>
        <span class="project-meta-value">Aneta Arct, Santiago Ortega, Agnieszka Gudowska, Karolina Skorb, Monika Gronowska, Magdalena Zagalska-Neubauer, Dorota Kotowska, Szymon M. Drobniak, Malgorzata Lagisz, Shinichi Nakagawa</span>
      </div>
      <div class="project-meta-item">
        <span class="project-meta-label">Published</span>
        <span class="project-meta-value">June 18, 2026</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="project-hero-graphic" aria-hidden="true">
    <img class="project-hero-bird" src="figures/site/geometric_world_bird_hero.png" alt="" />
  </div>
</div>

<div class="page-intro">
<p>
This book documents a reproducible comparative analysis of environmental variation and extra-pair paternity (EPP) in birds. The analysis uses population-level estimates of the proportion of sampled broods containing at least one extra-pair young and links them to environmental conditions, geography, species identity, phylogeny, and sampling structure.
</p>

<p>
The project is organised around three main environmental model groups: an environmental PCA model, a short-anomaly model, and a long-anomaly model. Each model group is fitted in two versions: a mean-only beta-binomial model and a location-scale beta-binomial model. All models include methodological controls for nest-box use and genetic marker type.
</p>
</div>

<div class="main-question-box">
  <strong>Main question</strong>
  <p>Do population-level EPP rates vary along broad environmental gradients related to temperature, precipitation, thermal variability, productivity, latitude, and distance to coast?</p>
</div>

<div class="structure-title">Website structure</div>

<div class="chapter-grid">

  <div class="chapter-card highlight-overview">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">1.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Environmental data sources</div>
      <p>
        Description of the climate, productivity, and geographic datasets used to characterise breeding-season environmental conditions.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./00_environmental_data_sources.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">2.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Data preparation</div>
      <p>
        Construction of the analytical dataset linking EPP records to sampling effort, breeding timing, location, and environmental predictors.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./01_data_preparation.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">3.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Taxonomy and phylogeny</div>
      <p>
        Taxonomic harmonisation and preparation of the phylogenetic covariance matrix used in the comparative models.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./02_taxonomy_matching.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">4.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Environmental PCA</div>
      <p>
        Six correlated environmental-geographic predictors are summarised into two broad axes: a thermal-geographic gradient and a wet-productivity gradient.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./04_pca_for_environmental_predictors.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">5.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Model structure and rationale</div>
      <p>
        Description of the beta-binomial framework, response structure, random effects, methodological controls, and the role of mean-only versus location-scale models.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./03_overall_model.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card highlight-main">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">6.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Main environmental models</div>
      <p>
        Three main model groups are fitted:
      </p>
      <ul>
        <li>Environmental PCA model (PC1 + PC2)</li>
        <li>Short anomaly model</li>
        <li>Long anomaly model</li>
      </ul>
      <p>
        Each group includes methodological controls and is fitted as both a mean-only and a location-scale model.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./05_location_scale_models.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card highlight-sensitivity">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">7.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Sensitivity models</div>
      <p>
        Sensitivity analyses replace the PCA axes with direct environmental-geographic predictors such as temperature, precipitation, thermal variability, NDVI, latitude, and distance to coast.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./06_sensitivity_models.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">8.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Location-scale models</div>
      <p>
        Exploratory models evaluate whether environmental and methodological predictors explain variation in the beta-binomial precision parameter.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./07_location_scale_models.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chapter-card">
    <div>
      <div class="chapter-number">9.</div>
      <div class="chapter-title">Figures</div>
      <p>
        Final figures, model summaries, and visual outputs used to interpret environmental effects and present the main results.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="chapter-link">
      <a href="./07_figures.html">Open chapter</a>
    </div>
  </div>

</div>

<div class="project-note">
</div>
